description: No sign-in needed. For timers made up on the spot (a label and a duration, started now) it makes a link that rings in the browser on the phone in the kitchen, one link per timer, and if the person signs in later those timers move to their phone. With the phone linked (the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app, ⋯ → Link an agent) it starts the timers on the phone itself, and the phone is alerted even when it is asleep. Saved presets, stopwatches, repeating buzzes, steps and idle (startNow false) timers need the phone link. For a whole saved meal use start_meal.

notify.description: Send one notification to the cook's phone that these timers were started. Default true — a timer the cook never learns about is a trap.

presets.description: Names or ids of saved presets to start (see list_cookbook). Each one's use count is bumped, as tapping it in the app would.

startNow.description: true runs them immediately. false creates them idle so the cook taps Start — this is what the app's Load button does.

rings.description: How many times the finish alarm repeats before giving up. Default 10.

sound.description: 'off' means vibrate and notification only. Only these two values do anything.

vibrate.description: Vibrate the phone when the timer finishes.

colour.description: The timer's card colour. Omit and it gets the next colour no timer on the board uses.

duration.description: How long, WITH A UNIT: '8m', '90s', '1h30m', '1.5 hours'. A number without a unit is rejected. Required unless 'steps' is given.

every.description: Buzz repeatedly at this interval WITHOUT shortening the timer, e.g. '5m' (minimum 5s). Use for 'stir every 5 minutes'. Do not combine with steps or manualFlips.

label.description: What is cooking, e.g. 'Rice'. Shown on the phone's lock-screen notification. Defaults to 'Timer'.

manualFlips.description: Enable a hand-logged flip list with no automatic buzzing; log flips later with control_timers action 'flip'. Do not combine with every or steps.

steps.description: Buzz at each stage boundary, e.g. ['2m','4m','4m'] for sear-2 then flip-every-4. Total run time is the SUM of the steps, so do not also send 'duration'. There is no buzz at the final boundary — the finish alert covers it. Do not combine with every or manualFlips.

stopwatch.description: Make a stopwatch instead of a countdown: it counts UP from 0, has no deadline and never rings. Give no duration, every, steps or manualFlips with it. Drive it with control_timers: start, pause (resume with start), flip = lap, reset, delete.

name: start_timers

outputSchema.description: Signed in: the timers now on the phone. With no sign-in: a link per timer (plans, and code/url of the first).

adjusted.description: Only when the asked-for time was up to 15 minutes too soon: the plan starts now and is ready later than asked. askedReadyAtMs / askedReadyAt is what was asked, lateMinutes how much too soon it was.

askedReadyAt.description: With movedToNext: the moment that had passed, ISO 8601 (UTC). (With adjusted it is inside adjusted.)

askedReadyAtMs.description: Only with planMade false: the ready time that was asked for.

askedReadyLocal.description: With movedToNext and a plain local time: what was asked (19:00, or 2026-11-20T19:00).

created.description: The timers now on the board.

elapsed.description: A stopwatch only: the time on its clock as m:ss.

elapsedMs.description: A stopwatch only: the time on its clock in milliseconds.

finishMayMove.description: Present with waitsForFlips: the finish time moves by however long each flip takes.

flips.description: How many flips have been logged.

kind.description: Only on a stopwatch (it counts up, has no deadline and never rings): remaining and duration mean nothing for it, read elapsed. Create one with start_timers stopwatch:true and drive it with control_timers (flag stopwatch).

laps.description: Full flip log; only with include:['laps'].

nextBuzz.description: Countdown to the next buzz, e.g. 'in 1:48'.

origin.description: Who last wrote it: app, mcp or server.

recorded.description: This run has been written to history.

reminders.description: How this timer buzzes before it finishes.

every.description: Interval as a duration string, when mode is 'interval'.

stepNames.description: Optional names the cook gave the stages on the phone (e.g. 'Cheese on'), parallel to steps; '' = unnamed. Set on the phone only.

ringing.description: The finish alarm is probably still sounding on the phone.

scheduledStartAt.description: When a scheduled dish starts, ISO 8601.

scheduledStartAtMs.description: When a scheduled dish starts, epoch ms.

state.description: 'scheduled' is a finish-together dish waiting for its start moment.

waitedMs.description: Total time this run has spent waiting for flips so far.

waitingForFlip.description: Holding at a flip right now (state 'paused'); nothing counts down until the cook flips. control_timers 'start' = ✓ Flipped.

waitingSince.description: When the current wait for a flip began (ISO).

waitsForFlips.description: kt-v35 flip-wait timer: it holds at every flip until the cook confirms, so endsAt is only a best case.

delivery.description: How recently the phone checked in, so you never imply it has seen this.

lastSyncAgo.description: Last sync in words, e.g. '2m ago'.

notified.description: A push about this change went out.

earliestReadyAtMs.description: Only with planMade false: the earliest the plan can be ready.

fromPresets.description: Presets that were used, with their new use counts.

links.description: Each dish that starts after another dish (also on the dish as startsAfter).

movedToNext.description: Only when the asked-for time had already passed: the plan is for the next time the clock reads that (normally tomorrow), not an error. askedReadyAt (or askedReadyLocal, when no time zone was known) is what was asked; the reply text says the day.

notMade.description: No sign-in only: how many of the timers were refused (the chat's limit); the text says why.

phoneAlert.description: Whether the paired device's backup alarm armed, and which device that is. armed:false is a real answer, not an error.

alarmsArmed.description: Finish alarms armed by this call.

armed.description: true only if a server alarm is set AND this phone can receive push.

device.description: Which device will ring: the phone app (Android or installed app), a browser tab (rings only while the tab stays open), no paired device, or one that has not said (older version).

pushedToPhone.description: A notification about this change was sent.

reason.description: Why nothing armed, in words worth repeating to the cook.

startRemindersArmed.description: Start reminders armed for scheduled dishes.

summary.description: One sentence naming the device that will ring, worth repeating to the cook as is.

willAlertWhileAsleep.description: true only when armed AND the device is the phone app. A browser tab or an unknown device is never promised.

planMade.description: True when a plan was made (code, url and the schedule are then present). False: the time was too soon by more than 15 minutes, nothing was made, and earliestReadyAtMs says when it can be ready; call again with startNow true or a later readyAt.

plans.description: No sign-in only: one entry per timer: code, url, name, readyAtMs.

readyLocal.description: Only when readyAt was a plain local clock time: that time (19:00, or 2026-11-23T19:00). The phone that opens the link fixes the real moment in its own time zone.

atMs.description: Absent when the plan was made from a plain local clock time: the phone fixes the real moment when it opens the link. Then localTime and minutesBeforeReady say when.

localTime.description: Only for a plan made from a plain local clock time: the wall-clock time, for example 5:40 PM.

minutesBeforeReady.description: Only for a plan made from a plain local clock time: how long before everything is ready this happens.

url.description: Open this on the phone in the kitchen.

warnings.description: Things worth saying out loud that are not failures.
